quiz.question: What does a union type in TypeScript allow you to do?

answers.answer: Combine two objects into one merged object
Allow a value to be one of several specified types
Create a new type that has all properties of multiple types
Convert a value from one type to another at runtime

quiz.explanation: A union type, written with the pipe | symbol, lets a variable hold a value of any one of the listed types. It does not merge objects or convert types.

quiz.question: What happens if you assign a boolean to a variable typed as string | number?

answers.answer: TypeScript silently converts it to a string
The value is stored as undefined
TypeScript reports a type error at compile time
It works fine because boolean is compatible with number

quiz.explanation: TypeScript enforces that only the types listed in the union can be assigned. Since boolean is not part of string | number, it produces a compile-time error.
